site.name: Dīvān-i Isfahan — Civic Register of the Naqsh-e Jahan
site.concept: The civic register and public-records office of Isfahan under the reign of Shah Abbas, publishing edicts, market hours, and notices of the Maydan.

card_pattern: Modules are square-ish cards framed by an ogee pointed-arch outline in cobalt with a thin gold filet inside. Card interiors are calm ivory with a single turquoise rule beneath the heading; a small Islamic-star seal sits in the upper-right corner. Body text is centered for civic notices, left-aligned for ledgers.
design_rules: Strict central axis on every page, with ornament concentrated at borders, spandrels, and around openings while interiors stay cream and quiet. Palette holds to cobalt, turquoise, gold, and ivory — oxblood appears only for emphasis on edicts and warnings. All ornament reads as cut-tile mosaic, never painted gradient.

pages.title: Dīvān-i Isfahan — Register of the Naqsh-e Jahan
pages.content_brief: Opening iwan-style hero introducing the Dīvān as the civic register seated at the northern arcade of the Maydan-e Naqsh-e Jahan. A central seal carries the date 1037 A.H. / 1628 C.E. Three columns beneath announce: a new edict from the Royal Court, the week's posted bazaar prices, and a notice concerning the Zayandeh-Rud canal works. A closing band lists the office hours: every day save Friday, from the second prayer to sunset.

pages.title: Edicts & Royal Decrees — Dīvān-i Isfahan
pages.content_brief: A ledger of currently-posted edicts (farmān) issued under the seal of the court. Entries include: 'On the regulation of caravan tolls between Kashan and Qom' (3rd of Rabi'-al-Awwal), 'On the appointment of Mirza Taqi as kalāntar of the silk-weavers' guild', and 'On the prohibition of unlicensed dyeing within the Bazaar-e Bozorg'. Each entry shows date, issuing authority, and a brief summary in plain civic prose.

pages.title: The Bazaar Register — Posted Prices & Weights
pages.content_brief: A weekly civic table of regulated prices at the Qaysarieh and adjacent caravanserais: wheat per man-e Tabriz, rice from Gilan, indigo cake, raw silk from Mazandaran, copper ingot. Standards of weight and measure are restated below — the man, the sang, the gaz — with a paragraph reminding merchants that inspections by the muhtasib occur on the 1st and 15th of each month.

pages.title: Public Works of the City — Canals, Bridges, Caravanserais
pages.content_brief: A list of ongoing civic works: the dredging of the Madi-ye Niāsarm canal, repairs to the Allahverdi Khan Bridge (Si-o-se-pol) parapets, and the new caravanserai gate near the Darb-e Kushk quarter. Each item gives the master-builder, the responsible quarter (mahalle), and the expected completion. A short paragraph thanks the citizens of the Jolfa quarter for their contribution to the bridge timberwork.

pages.title: Petitions & Hearings — Office of the Dīvānbegi
pages.content_brief: Instructions for citizens wishing to submit a petition (arzeh-dāsht). Petitions are received in the outer courtyard each morning save Friday; hearings are held by the Dīvānbegi every Wednesday afternoon. Required: name, quarter, trade, and seal of two witnesses. A note clarifies that disputes among the Armenian community of New Jolfa are heard by their own kalāntar before reaching the Dīvān.

pages.title: Visiting the Dīvān — Hours, Address, Conduct
pages.content_brief: Practical guidance for visitors. The office is located beneath the northern arcade of the Maydan-e Naqsh-e Jahan, between the Qaysarieh gate and the Mosque of Sheikh Lotfollah. Hours: daily from after the dawn prayer until sunset, closed Fridays and on the festival of Nowruz. Visitors are asked to leave riding-animals at the southern caravanserai and to observe quiet conduct within the courtyard.
